description: Example transmitter-receptor profile: the sign of a synapse depends on its receptor and on developmental context, not on the transmitter alone.

receptors.name: ionotropic_glutamate
receptors.citation: AMPA-type cation channels; Traynelis et al. 2010, Pharmacol Rev

receptors.name: glutamate_gated_chloride
receptors.citation: GluCl, an inhibitory glutamate receptor of invertebrates; Cully et al. 1994, Nature

receptors.name: sign_inverting_metabotropic_glutamate
receptors.citation: mGluR6-like: glutamate closes a cation channel (hyperpolarisation); Nakajima et al. 1993, J Biol Chem

receptors.name: gaba_a
receptors.citation: chloride channel; depolarising in immature neurons (high internal chloride); Ben-Ari 2002, Nat Rev Neurosci

receptors.name: glycine
receptors.citation: chloride channel with the same developmental switch; Ben-Ari 2002, Nat Rev Neurosci

receptors.name: nicotinic
receptors.citation: nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (cation channel); Albuquerque et al. 2009, Physiol Rev

transmitters.quantity: list of transmitters of the example
transmitters.note: An illustrative list for the example, not a statement about a species.

receptors.quantity: receptor classes, signs and developmental contexts of the example
receptors.note: Illustrative example: each receptor carries its own citation (Traynelis 2010, Cully, Hardie 1989, Albuquerque, Ben-Ari 2002 and others), none of which has been checked against the paper.
